title: Module-object and ringed-site derived internal Hom agree
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its pro-étale site taken small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and put $B=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], a commutative ring object of abelian sheaves with the sheafified pointwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$ [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]; write $B_{\mathrm{sec}}$ for its section-ring sheaf. Let $\mathcal A$ be the category of $B$-module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(B_{\mathrm{sec}})$ the category of sheaves of $B_{\mathrm{sec}}$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $F:\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal M$ the equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], which leaves underlying abelian sheaves, sections and morphisms unchanged. Let $D(F)$ be its termwise extension to the ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and identify the K-flat derived relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] with the ordinary ringed-site K-flat derived tensor through the comparison of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. Let $\operatorname{RHom}^{\mathcal A}_B$ be the derived internal Hom of $D(\mathcal A)$, defined as the right adjoint of this derived relative tensor in [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], and let $R\mathcal Hom_{B_{\mathrm{sec}}}$ be the functorial K-injective sheaf-Hom model of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then for all $K,N\in D(\mathcal A)$ there are isomorphisms
$$D(F)\bigl(\operatorname{RHom}_{B}^{\mathcal A}(K,N)\bigr)\cong R\mathcal Hom_{B_{\mathrm{sec}}}(D(F)K,D(F)N),$$
natural in $K$ (contravariantly) and $N$, which carry the evaluation morphism $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_B\operatorname{RHom}^{\mathcal A}_B(K,N)\to N$, transported by $D(F)$ and the tensor comparison, to the ringed-site evaluation $D(F)K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{B_{\mathrm{sec}}}R\mathcal Hom_{B_{\mathrm{sec}}}(D(F)K,D(F)N)\to D(F)N$. For every object $U$ of $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, restricting these isomorphisms to the slice site $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] gives the corresponding isomorphisms for the ring object $B|_U$ and its section-ring sheaf.

proof.text: The internal-to-sectionwise equivalence is the one fixed in the statement: it preserves the underlying abelian sheaves, sections, restriction maps and morphisms. The relative tensor comparison node gives a natural isomorphism between internal relative tensor and the ordinary sheaf-module tensor, identifies the units, and says that the equivalence is exact and preserves and reflects flat modules and K-flat complexes. Thus applying the termwise functor D(F) to K-flat representatives gives a natural comparison D(F)(K tensor_B^L L) with D(F)K tensor_{B_sec}^L D(F)L, including the unit comparison.

proof.text: For fixed K, the module-object derived internal Hom is the right adjoint of K tensor_B^L minus by the layer-B clause of the derived tensor-Hom definition. Transport this adjunction across the exact equivalence D(F) and the tensor comparison from Step 1. The transported functor D(F)(RHom_B^A(K,-)) is therefore right adjoint to D(F)K tensor_{B_sec}^L minus, with counit equal to the image of the module-object evaluation under D(F) and the tensor comparison.

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal O=B_{\mathrm{sec}}$, a sheaf of commutative rings on the small site $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, and $H(L,M)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M)$ for the functorial K-injective model of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. This step shows that $H(K,-)$ is right adjoint to $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}-$, naturally in $K$; this is the statement of Stacks 08J9 that the currying isomorphism 'recovers (equation-internal-hom) on taking $H^0(\mathcal C,-)$'. For $A,K,N\in D(\mathcal O)$ compose the natural isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(A,H(K,N))\cong H^0(\mathcal C,H(A,H(K,N)))\cong H^0(\mathcal C,H(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}K,N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}K,N).$$
The first and third are [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] (canonical and natural in both variables, by its proof's pre/postcomposition equation), applied to the pairs $(A,H(K,N))$ and $(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}K,N)$; the middle one is $H^0(\mathcal C,-)$ of the currying isomorphism $H(A,H(K,N))\cong H(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}K,N)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], natural in $A,K,N$. Finally exchange the tensor factors: choose K-flat representatives $P$ of $A$ and $P'$ of $K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex]; both $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes P')$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(P'\otimes P)$ represent the derived tensor in either order, and the Koszul exchange $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ on $P^p\otimes P'^q$ commutes with the differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] (because $(p+1)q\equiv pq+q$ and $p(q+1)\equiv pq+p$ mod 2) and is natural in chain maps, giving $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}K\cong K\otimes^{\mathbf L}A$ naturally. The result is a bijection $\psi_{A,K,N}:\operatorname{Hom}(A,H(K,N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}A,N)$ natural in all three variables, i.e. a parametrized adjunction $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}-\dashv H(K,-)$. The ringed-site evaluation $\mathrm{ev}_{K,N}:K\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(K,N)\to N$ of the statement is its counit $\psi_{H(K,N),K,N}(\mathrm{id})$, as in the defining adjunction (equation-internal-hom) of Stacks Section 08J7. No existence of a right adjoint is presupposed here, so nothing is circular.

source.place: Section 08J7 (section-internal-hom, equation-internal-hom), Lemma 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U, global clause) and Lemma 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom, 'which recovers (equation-internal-hom) on taking H^0')

proof.text: Write $G(K',N')=D(F)\operatorname{RHom}^{\mathcal A}_B(D(F)^{-1}K',D(F)^{-1}N')$ for a quasi-inverse of the equivalence $D(F)$. By Step 2 there are bijections $\varphi_{A,K',N'}:\operatorname{Hom}(A,G(K',N'))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K'\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}A,N')$, natural in all three variables, whose counit is the image of the module-object evaluation under $D(F)$ and the tensor comparison of Step 1. By Step 3, $\psi$ is a second such family for $H$. For fixed $K',N'$ the composite $\psi^{-1}\varphi:\operatorname{Hom}(-,G(K',N'))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(-,H(K',N'))$ is natural in $A$, so by the Yoneda lemma it is postcomposition with a unique isomorphism $\theta_{K',N'}=\psi^{-1}\varphi(\mathrm{id}_{G(K',N')}):G(K',N')\to H(K',N')$, with inverse $\varphi^{-1}\psi(\mathrm{id})$. Naturality of $\varphi$ and $\psi$ in $K'$ (contravariant) and $N'$ makes $\theta$ natural in both. Since $\varphi(\mathrm{id})$ and $\psi(\mathrm{id})$ are the two counits and $\psi(\theta)=\varphi(\mathrm{id})$, naturality of $\psi$ in $A$ gives $\mathrm{ev}\circ(K'\otimes^{\mathbf L}\theta)=$ the transported module-object evaluation; $\theta$ is the unique morphism with this property. Taking $K'=D(F)K$, $N'=D(F)N$ gives the displayed isomorphism with the stated evaluation normalization and naturality.

source.place: Section 08J7, equation-internal-hom and the Yoneda uniqueness remark following it

proof.text: Let $U$ be an object of $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$. The slice site $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}/U$ is small, and by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] restriction keeps sections: $M|_U(V/U)=M(V)$, also for the ring object, so $B|_U$ is a commutative ring object of abelian sheaves on the slice whose section-ring sheaf is $B_{\mathrm{sec}}|_U=\mathcal O_U$, and $F(M)|_U=F_U(M|_U)$ with both sides the same sheaf, where $F_U$ is the equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] for $B|_U$. Restriction of modules is exact [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], so it acts termwise on derived categories and $D(F)(-)|_U=D(F_U)((-)|_U)$. Steps 1--4 use only the general-site nodes [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]; on the slice they give the ringed-site parametrized adjunction for $H_U=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}$, the module-object internal Hom $\operatorname{RHom}^{\mathcal A_U}_{B|_U}$ as a right adjoint of the derived relative tensor over $B|_U$ (by transporting $H_U$ through $D(F_U)$ and the tensor comparison when it is not already given), and the unique evaluation-normalized isomorphism $\theta^U:D(F_U)\operatorname{RHom}^{\mathcal A_U}_{B|_U}(K',N')\cong H_U(D(F_U)K',D(F_U)N')$. Let $\rho$ be the restriction isomorphism $H(L,M)|_U\cong H_U(L|_U,M|_U)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], compatible with successive restrictions. Define the module-object restriction comparison $r_U$ by $D(F_U)(r_U)=(\theta^U)^{-1}\circ\rho\circ\theta|_U$; then by construction $\theta|_U$ corresponds to $\theta^U$ under $r_U$ and $\rho$, which is the slice clause. For $V\to U$ the cocycle condition for $r$ follows by substituting the definitions: $(\theta^V)^{-1}\rho_{U\to V}\theta^U|_V\circ((\theta^U)^{-1}\rho_{X\to U}\theta|_U)|_V=(\theta^V)^{-1}\rho_{U\to V}(\rho_{X\to U})|_V\theta|_V=(\theta^V)^{-1}\rho_{X\to V}\theta|_V$, using the relocalization identification $(\mathcal C/U)/(V/U)=\mathcal C/V$ of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].
